Synergism of a new beta-lactam inhibitor (PS-5) in antimicrobial activity with various beta-lactam antibiotics against beta-lactams-resistant Gram-negative microorganisms.
PS-5 is a novel antibiotic that shows a synergistic effect in the combination with penicillin and cephalospirins in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synergism of PS5 with penicillin or cephalosporin in the treatment of beta-lactam resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
the synergistic action of PS-5 in combination with pen-icillins against E. coli and with cephalos-porins against P. vulgaris, S. marcescens, C. freundii, E. cloacae, P. morganii and E. aerogenes.
the synergism of PS5 with penicillin and cephalosprin against beta-lactams resistant Gram-negative bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PS-5 showed significant synergism with penicillin against beta-lacta-resistant E. coli, and with cephalosprins against beta-lactan-resistant Proteus vulgaris and Serratia marcens.
PS-5 is synergistic with penicillin and cephalosprin against Gram-negative bacteria, but the synergism is not so strong as to be useful clinically.

PS-5 showed synergism in combination with various penicillin and cephalosprin antibiotics against beta-lactm-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, and that the synergism was more pronounced in combination with penictillins than with cephalosprins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PS-5 showed synergism in antimicrobials action with penicillines or cephalosporines against beta-lactanase producing Gram-negative bacteria.
the synergistic effect of PS-5 in combination with peni-cillins was more significant than that with cephalos- porins.
the combination of PS-5 and beta-lactam antibiotics was synergistic against beta-lactams resistant strains of Gram-negative bacteria.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the PS-5-penicillin or PS-5-cephalosporin combination may be effective in the treatment of infections caused by beta-lactam resistant Gram-negative bacteria, particularly those caused by E. coli, S. marcescens and P. vulgaris.

PS-5 can be combined with beta-lactam antibiotics for synergistic effects against beta-lactams-resistant Gram-negative bacteria in vitro.
